The two are variant forms of the same Sanskrit word for the Jina; the Pāśupata homonym stays a separate definition on trm:tirthakara.
Both are the mendicant's rainy-season retreat undertaken so as not to harm beings on the roads; the rules and the festivals attached differ.
Both close or crown the rains with a communal act of reconciliation (Jain mutual forgiveness; Buddhist invitation to admonition); not the same rite.

Kundakunda's standpoint of ultimate reality plays the role of the ultimate level (P1) in relation to a conventional level used for teaching; it describes an individual pure soul and does not declare the world unreal, so only an analogy is asserted.
Both are the conventional level through which the ultimate is taught; the Jain standpoint remains a true partial view (naya), not an appearance.
